clue.text: Planned how to reverse effects of emancipation?

definitions.text: how to reverse effects of emancipation?
definitions.meaning: read as DE- plus LIBERATE, to undo a setting free

explanation.surface: Someone asks how the results of freeing slaves might be undone, a plotted scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: DE- as an undoing prefix on 'liberate' would reverse an emancipation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something planned is done intentionally, which is the adjective sense of the word.

clue.text: Intermittently door seems to create draughts

indicators.note: taking letters on and off, every other one of the words door seems

explanation.surface: A badly fitting door lets in cold currents of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is an old word for a measured drink of medicine, a single dose.

clue.text: Bending out of Florida's capital towards northern city

indicators.note: the following letter is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: bending a limb is flexing it

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word Florida's

parts.note: towards gives the preposition to

explanation.surface: A traveller heads away from Tallahassee, the capital of Florida, towards a city up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florida's capital' tempts with Tallahassee; it is just the letter F, removed from FLEXING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lexington is a city in Kentucky, also a town in Massachusetts.

clue.text: Book editor, it seems, reworked collection of fairy tales?

indicators.note: material that is reworked is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor reshapes a book of fairy tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' rearranges B plus EDITOR plus ITSEEMS into the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales told to children at lights-out are often fairy tales, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Carry out repairs to houses on the dot

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a point is a dot

explanation.surface: A builder fixes houses exactly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the dot' reads as one phrase meaning punctually, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Repointing is renewing the mortar between bricks, a routine repair to a house's walls.

clue.text: Heard characteristic noise made by second-hand car perhaps

indicators.note: heard says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait, a noise is a din

explanation.surface: A used car makes a recognisable rattle.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIT plus DIN, spoken together, sound like the hyphenated phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old car handed over as part payment for a new one, so an example of a used vehicle.

clue.text: Singer and composer at heart

indicators.note: only the heart of the name is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: William Walton was an English composer

explanation.surface: A vocalist and a composer share a heartfelt bond.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a voice in the low female or high male range.

clue.text: Owner of estate set out after fixing motor finally

indicators.note: the first word takes in, or fixes inside itself, the next piece

parts.note: to set out a table is to lay it, so laid

indicators.note: the final letter of the word motor

explanation.surface: A landowner leaves after repairing his car engine.
explanation.walkthrough: R, from 'motor finally', goes inside LAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scottish term for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Improving old song that's missing start and finish

indicators.note: the song loses its first letter

parts.note: an anthem is a song
finish means end

explanation.surface: An old tune gets better though it lacks its beginning and ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing start and finish' seems to trim both ends of the song; only 'missing start' acts on ANTHEM, and 'finish' supplies END.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is recovering after illness is getting better, so the idiom means improving.

clue.text: Jumper covers our football club supporter's mascot

indicators.note: the first word wraps round, or covers, the next

parts.note: a flea is an insect that jumps
taken as written
a lover is a fan or supporter

explanation.surface: A fan's sweater bears the club emblem as a good-luck charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater (the British word for a pullover) but is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare plant is a traditional good-luck charm, like a mascot.

clue.text: Understand roly-poly dessert with unknown ingredient is made more spicy

indicators.note: the unknown is put into the first word as an ingredient goes into a dish

parts.note: to see is to understand
X is an unknown quantity in algebra

indicators.note: roly-poly suggests rolling over, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A cook adds a mystery ingredient to a jam roly-poly to liven it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Roly-poly is a British rolled jam pudding; here 'roly-poly' rolls PUD over to give DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex something up is the informal idiom for making it more exciting or racy.

clue.text: I love a film about men in uniform

indicators.note: the film goes round the men

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as of condensation
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Someone declares a passion for a movie about soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the lover's own declaration: one who loves might say 'I love'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given to romance and courtship would say these words, so they stand for such a lover.

clue.text: Kept secret in St Ives: unexpected closure of Tate

indicators.note: something unexpected is out of the usual order, so the letters are shuffled
the closing letter of the word Tate

explanation.surface: News is hushed up in St Ives that the Tate gallery there will unexpectedly shut.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives in Cornwall has a branch of the Tate gallery. 'unexpected' scrambles IN plus STIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitive information is classified, held back from the public.

clue.text: Dickensian character — good, though outwardly ill-mannered

indicators.note: the first word is outside, surrounding the next

parts.note: ill-mannered means rude

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure is virtuous though rough in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel.

clue.text: Dish that is divided for starters

parts.note: something divided is cut; for starters puts it first, before the other piece

explanation.surface: A dish is split up for the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' looks like food; it means an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is slang for an attractive person, and a cutie is the same.

clue.text: Expert found line missing from finished section of Bible

indicators.note: the line is taken out of the word for finished

parts.note: finished means complete
NT, the New Testament, is a section of the Bible

explanation.surface: A scholar finds a line absent from a completed part of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent means capable and skilled, close to expert in sense.

clue.text: Retired senator's goal: to visit one of the states

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: SEN is an abbreviation for senator
the net is the goal in football
to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A senator, now retired, has the goal of touring one American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns SEN plus NET, giving TENNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Synopsis of something a northerner said to one working

parts.note: summat is northern English dialect for something
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman tells a worker something that sums things up.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMAT is how 'something' is said in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A summation is a summing-up, a short overview of the main points.

clue.text: Devised smart name for old guards

indicators.note: a devised thing is worked out anew, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone thought up a smart name for veteran sentries.
explanation.definitionFit: Men-at-arms were medieval soldiers, often serving as armed guards.

clue.text: Reconsider entering half a dozen in further examination

indicators.note: the six goes into the exam word

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken again
VI is the Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: Six students sit a retake to think again.
explanation.definitionFit: To revisit a question is to look at it again, to reconsider it.

clue.text: Notices damaged part

indicators.note: a damaged thing is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone notices a broken component.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part or segment of a whole.

clue.text: Well-known American arrested by FBI agent

indicators.note: the American is held inside the agent's word

parts.note: a fed is US slang for an FBI agent

explanation.surface: A well-known American is picked up by the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Famed means celebrated or famous.

clue.text: Some hear mountain bird

indicators.note: some people say the bird's name aloud so that it is heard like the mountain

parts.note: Mount Ida is a mountain in Crete and in Turkey

explanation.surface: Some people hear a mountain bird calling.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's name is pronounced 'eye-der' by many, matching IDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its down.

clue.text: Who may be caught in CID operation?

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words CID operation

explanation.surface: A question about who might be nabbed in a police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police; a drug taker might well be caught in one of its raids.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper is a drug user, or someone doping a horse or athlete, who may be caught.

clue.text: Hesitate to leave, sick at heart

indicators.note: the sickness is placed at the heart of the leaving word

parts.note: to vacate is to leave
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone sick at heart is reluctant to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver or dither, to hesitate between choices.

clue.text: Lines written by poet, say, in English city

indicators.note: the example goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A poet writes verses in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English' tempts as E; the whole 'English city' is ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, lines a poet writes for the dead.

clue.text: Put into words, using special delivery

definitions.meaning: to state or convey in speech or writing

explanation.surface: Someone says something by sending it urgently.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to voice it, and an express delivery is a special fast one.

clue.text: Account given by popular speaker

parts.note: something popular is in
a voice is a speaker, as in 'a voice of reason'

explanation.surface: A popular orator gives a report.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill, an account of what is owed.

clue.text: Circle Line on time? Right

indicators.note: on places the circle and line after the time, as across entries run

parts.note: O is round, a circle
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Is the London Underground's Circle line running on schedule? Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it splits into O and RY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tories are the British right-wing party, so the political right.

clue.text: Going from place to place, queen visits Italian island and French city

indicators.note: the queen goes into the city as a visitor

parts.note: Nancy is a city in eastern France
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A touring queen visits an Italian island and a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerancy is the state of travelling around, never settled.
